rationale: Each horizontal pair becomes one cell: [1,1] yields 1 and [3,3] yields 3, while [0,1] and [3,0] yield 0. Select uniform non-background pairs.
Each 3x3 block becomes 5 if occupied: the first demonstration's sparse upper-left block and solid upper-third block both yield 5; empty blocks yield 0.
Reduce horizontal pairs by the most common colour including background: [2,2] yields 2, [3,3] yields 3, and tied [0,1] or [1,0] yields 0.
Reduce vertical pairs by the most common colour including background: equal 1s or 2s retain their colour; the second demonstration's pairs containing one zero and one nonzero all yield 0.
Only solid non-background 2x2 blocks retain their colour. In the second demonstration, four 3s yield 3, while the block with three 1s and one zero yields 0.
Only uniform non-background 3x3 blocks survive. The first demonstration retains solid 3 and 2 blocks, while its seven-1 block containing two zeros yields 0.
Each 2x3 block retains its colour only when all six cells share a nonzero colour. The second demonstration's incomplete 3 block yields 0, while solid 2 and 1 blocks yield 2 and 1.
Any nonzero cell in a 2x3 block produces 5; empty blocks produce 0. The third demonstration's lower-right block contains only one 1 yet yields 5.
Reduce each 2x3 block to its most common non-background colour. The first demonstration's upper-left block has two 1s and four zeros but yields 1; empty blocks yield 0.
Each vertical pair retains its colour only if both cells share a nonzero colour. The second demonstration preserves [1,1] and [2,2] but maps [1,0] and [0,2] to 0.
